summary.short: The State Council regulation controls exports of dual-use items (goods, technology, services and related data) through licensing, end-user and end-use management, and control and watch lists, with penalties for violations. It applies from 1 December 2024 and repeals four earlier export control regulations.
summary.long: Issued as State Council Decree No. 792 (adopted 18 September 2024, promulgated 30 September 2024, effective 1 December 2024), the regulation implements the Export Control Law for dual-use items: goods, technology, services and related data with civil uses and military or weapons-of-mass-destruction relevance. Chapter 2 covers policy, a dual-use item list, temporary controls on items outside the list (each for up to two years), and prohibitions on specific items or destinations. Chapter 3 requires licences for listed items: single licences (valid up to one year), general licences (valid up to three years, for exporters with an internal compliance system and export record) or registration-based export certificates. Single-licence applications are decided within 45 working days, and changes to non-critical elements within 20 working days. Exports must be presented to customs with the licence. Chapter 3 also covers end-user and end-use statements and the watch list and control list of importers and end users, against which transactions may be banned or restricted. Chapter 4 sets supervision and inspection powers. Chapter 5 provides for warnings, confiscation, fines and criminal liability. Chapter 6 covers transit, re-export and overseas-made items containing Chinese-origin items, and repeals four earlier regulations on nuclear, missile, biological and chemical dual-use export controls.
